raw_response:
I will keep the farm simple and steady this year because I am farming only 8.5 mu, I have family labor limits, and some people work off-farm. I will not spread myself too thin. I will put part of the land into the wheat-maize cycle because it is familiar, fits my well irrigation, and gives me grain in two seasons from the same ground. I will keep the rest in sunflower because it suits my usual planting pattern and needs less water and labor than trying to push all the land into higher-input crops. I will use better seed where it helps me get stable yield, but I will not chase very heavy fertilizer or too many sprays because that raises cost and work. For wheat, I will feed it enough to hold a solid stand through winter and grain filling. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same land and manage it more strongly because maize responds well to fertilizer and water. For sunflower, I will keep inputs moderate, give one irrigation if needed from the well, and protect it with limited pesticide use. I will mainly use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and easier to manage on a small farm.
